Case: Working login screen is displayed when a stale auth link is opened by a signed-out user
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is signed out. A previously bookmarked or shared URL for /u/login/identifier contains a stale or expired Auth0 state parameter (tab left open 2+ hours, or URL copied from an old session).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-000 · AC1
  • Traceability / AC Source: "Given a bookmarked /u/login/identifier, a page refreshed mid-login, or a tab left open 2+ hours, when it is opened or submitted, then the user lands on a working login screen and never sees invalid_request."
Test Steps:
1. Copy a login URL that contains a stale state parameter (e.g., from a session started over 2 hours ago).
  2. Open the URL in a browser where the user is not currently signed in.
  3. Observe the page that loads.
Expected:
• The working login screen (Step 1 — Email or username field) is displayed.
  • No "Oops!, something went wrong" message is shown.
  • No "invalid_request" error code is visible.
  • No tracking ID error string is displayed.
BDD: Given a signed-out user has a stale auth link with an expired state parameter, When the user opens the link, Then the working login screen is displayed with no invalid_request error

Case: User is redirected directly to the app when a stale auth link is opened while already signed in
Description:
• Pre-condition: User is currently signed in to SleekFlow. A stale or expired auth URL for /u/login/identifier is opened (e.g., bookmarked URL with old state).
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-000 · AC1
  • Traceability / AC Source: "the user lands on a working login screen (or straight in the app if already signed in) and never sees invalid_request."
Test Steps:
1. Sign in to SleekFlow successfully in the browser.
  2. Open a stale/bookmarked auth URL that contains an expired state parameter.
  3. Observe where the user is redirected.
Expected:
• The user is redirected directly to the SleekFlow app dashboard (not the login screen).
  • No "Oops!, something went wrong" error page is shown.
  • No "invalid_request" error is visible at any point.
BDD: Given a user is already signed in and opens a stale auth link, When the page loads, Then the user is taken straight into the app without seeing any error

Case: invalid_request error page is no longer shown when a login page is loaded without a valid state parameter
Description:
• Pre-condition: P0-1 fix has been deployed (Auth0 Application Login URI or Tenant Login URI configured). User navigates to /u/login/identifier with no valid state parameter.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-000 · AC1, AC2
  • Traceability / AC Source: AC2: "Currently, a login page opened without a valid state shows 'Oops!, something went wrong' + invalid_request + tracking ID. After P0-1, this must never occur."
Test Steps:
1. Navigate directly to sso.sleekflow.io/u/login/identifier with no state parameter in the URL.
  2. Observe the page response.
  3. Check for any error messages or error codes.
Expected:
• A functional login screen is displayed (Email or username field visible).
  • The text "Oops!, something went wrong" is NOT present on the page.
  • The string "invalid_request" is NOT visible anywhere.
  • No tracking ID string (e.g., "Tracking ID: ...") is displayed.
BDD: Given a login URL is opened with no valid state parameter after P0-1 fix deployment, When the page loads, Then no invalid_request error page is shown and a working login screen appears

Case: Stale auth link recovery applies to sign-up, password reset, and email verification pages
Description:
• Pre-condition: P0-1 fix deployed. User is signed out. Stale/stateless URLs exist for /u/signup, /u/reset-password, and /u/email-verification.
  • Source: sleekflow-login-signup-000 · AC1
  • Traceability / AC Source: Context: "This applies to ALL auth pages: login, sign-up, reset, verification."
Test Steps:
1. Open a stale URL for the sign-up page (/u/signup/identifier) with an expired or missing state parameter.
  2. Observe the resulting page — confirm no error page shown.
  3. Open a stale URL for the password reset page with an expired or missing state parameter.
  4. Observe the resulting page — confirm no error page shown.
  5. Open a stale URL for the email verification page with an expired or missing state parameter.
  6. Observe the resulting page — confirm no error page shown.
Expected:
• Each auth page (sign-up, reset, verification) loads a usable UI when accessed with a stale state parameter.
  • None of the pages shows "Oops!, something went wrong".
  • None of the pages shows "invalid_request" or a tracking ID error string.
BDD: Given stale auth links exist for sign-up, reset, and verification pages, When a signed-out user opens each link, Then every page loads a working screen with no invalid_request error
